symptom: The public VII stay-calendar endpoint returns HTTP 503 supplier_unavailable for published vacation sites 2004 and 2566, while the exact stay-quote path for site 2004 and room 3422 returns a valid available quote.
expected_behavior: For a published vacation whose availability is managed online, the calendar returns authoritative nightly room inventory, minimum-night and arrival-closure data; exact stay quote remains authoritative before booking.
environment: VII public releases v658 through v660 at vii.spaplus.co on 2026-10-25, supplier API version documented as 1.1 at bizonline.co.il/api/ai/vii/Vii-Frontend.html.

steps: GET public stay-calendar for site 2004 from 2026-10-25 through 2026-11-24 with two guests.
GET the same public stay-calendar request for site 2566.
POST an exact one-night stay quote for site 2004, room 3422 and two guests.
reproduction.evidence: Both calendar requests returned HTTP 503; the quote returned HTTP 200 with available status, total 1400, one night, roomIDs [3422] and onlineBooking true.

observations.observation: The official current documentation still defines GET vacations/{siteID}/calendar with from, till and optional roomID and returns rooms[].dates[] with availableUnitCount, availableUnits, minNights and closedArrival.
observations.evidence: Official Vii Frontend API page fetched successfully on 2026-10-25.

observations.observation: The local adapter calls that documented GET path but collapses upstream non-2xx, transport errors and strict parser failures into the same public supplier_unavailable response.
The supplier token, publication inventory and exact vacancy path are functional for the same site and date family.
observations.evidence: Public stay-quote succeeded for site 2004 and room 3422 while the calendar request failed.

observations.observation: v659 classified both calendar failures as supplier_transport before any Response was received; runtime duration was 831 ms for site 2004 and 1200 ms for site 2566, excluding the 20-second timeout path.
The calendar adapter alone used redirect:error while the working supplier calls followed redirects. Changing only that behavior to redirect:follow made both public calendars return HTTP 200.
observations.evidence: v660 production probes returned full 31-day calendars for sites 2004 and 2566, including minNights and closedArrival; the exact quote remained HTTP 200 and total 1400.

hypotheses.mechanism: The supplier calendar returns HTTP success with a legal response shape that the local strict parser rejects.
hypotheses.prediction: A sanitized diagnostic will show upstream HTTP 200 and identify a response-field representation mismatch.
hypotheses.discriminating_test: Capture upstream status, content type, top-level keys and field-type summary without credentials or private data.
hypotheses.result: Rejected: v659 failed before a Response object or parser execution.

hypotheses.mechanism: The calendar request receives a non-2xx provider response because the request contract or per-site calendar capability differs from the exact vacancy path.
hypotheses.prediction: A sanitized diagnostic will show a non-2xx upstream status and safe provider error classification for both sites.
hypotheses.discriminating_test: Record upstream status and provider error_code for the documented calendar request, then compare with the working vacancy request.
hypotheses.result: Rejected: no upstream HTTP response was delivered to the adapter in v659.

hypotheses.mechanism: Shared authentication, publication lookup or network access is failing before the supplier calendar is reached.
hypotheses.prediction: The exact quote and calendar would fail together for the same site and request window.
hypotheses.discriminating_test: Compare same-release public calendar and quote results for site 2004.
hypotheses.result: Rejected provisionally because stay-quote succeeded with the same token source and publication inventory.

hypotheses.mechanism: The calendar adapter's redirect:error policy turns the supplier calendar's infrastructure redirect into an immediate fetch exception, unlike the working supplier calls.
hypotheses.prediction: Following the redirect will produce an authoritative HTTP response without changing endpoint, authentication or request data.
hypotheses.discriminating_test: Change only redirect handling, publish once, and repeat both calendars plus the unchanged exact quote.
hypotheses.result: Supported: both calendars changed from supplier_transport to HTTP 200 with authoritative 31-day data, and the exact quote remained available at 1400.

fix.change: Follow the documented supplier calendar redirect like the other working VII supplier requests, while preserving fixed origin, Bearer authentication, timeout, strict schema validation and safe diagnostics.
fix.evidence: Public v660 returned HTTP 200 calendars for sites 2004 and 2566; site 2566 returned one room and 31 dated records with minNights and closedArrival; exact quote site 2004 room 3422 returned HTTP 200, available, one night and total 1400.

regression_checks: Public site 2004 calendar returned HTTP 200 with authoritative inventory and minimum-night data.
Public site 2566 calendar returned HTTP 200 with one room and 31 dates.
Public site 2004 room 3422 quote remained HTTP 200, available and 1400.
authorization_boundary: Read-only supplier documentation and public probes are allowed. A bounded diagnostic and repair may be published under the user's existing explicit authorization, but no supplier write, booking, payment, lead, message or secret exposure is allowed.
